Hi all —

Thanks for the interest in a live walkthrough for the pilot. We want to lock a time that works for US/EU/APAC participants and avoid surprises from upcoming daylight saving changes. Two candidate slots (converted to local times below):

Option A — Wed Mar 10, 16:00 UTC
  - London: 16:00 GMT
  - San Francisco: 08:00 PST
  - Sydney (AEDT): 03:00 +11 (Thu Mar 11)

Option B — Thu Mar 11, 09:00 UTC
  - London: 09:00 GMT
  - San Francisco: 01:00 PST
  - Sydney (AEDT): 20:00 +11

Quick notes: US daylight saving starts on Sun Mar 14 this year — that will shift future recurring meetings for US attendees by +1 hour. Australia (and NZ) have different changeover dates in April, so any follow-ups scheduled across that cutover can appear to move in recipients' calendars. To avoid confusion we can:
  - Send invites with explicit UTC in the title + local conversions in the body; or
  - Lock the meeting time in UTC and add a friendly note about DST effects for follow-ups.

Please reply with preferred option and any strict no-go windows (esp. for Sydney/Auckland teammates). I can send a single confirmed invite in UTC so calendar clients convert consistently.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake

Hi Liam —

Short answer on the invite behavior: standard calendar invites are timezone-aware and clients convert to local time when they accept. The tricky part is recurring meetings created before/after DST changeover — depending on the client, the local time can appear to shift for some attendees. To be safe for a one-off demo and any follow-up we recommend:

1) Send the confirmed invite with the meeting anchored to UTC (e.g., "Thu Mar 11 09:00 UTC / 20:00 AEDT") in the title.
2) Include explicit conversions in the body (UTC + local for common regions).
3) For follow-ups scheduled across Mar 14 / early April, we call them out in the invite description and suggest a re-check.

Jordan — if the team prefers Option B I can send the invite and include a Zoom link, record permission, and an agenda. Ben — can you join as the solutions SME?

—Marissa
